messages.subject: Survey Design - Random Point Placement
messages.body_plain:
Dear List

I am using Distance 5 to design a point transect survey for woodland birds.
I would like to use a simple random design for placement of my points but
at the moment I tend to end up with overlapping plots.  I know that this
problem can be avoided if you plot points by hand but was interested to
know if there was a way to stop sampler overlap using Distance to design
the survey, other than by using a systematic grid design.

Many thanks
----------------------
Catherine Davey
School of Biological Sciences
University of Bristol
Woodland Road
Bristol BS8 1UG

Catheri...@bris.ac.uk

--

messages.subject: Re: Survey Design - Random Point Placement
messages.body_plain:
Personally, I would use a systematic design.  If you really don't want
to do that, you might want to take a look at chapter 7 of the advanced
distance sampling book, e.g. fig 7.2.  You could achieve this by
generating a systematic design where the plots don't quite overlap, then
selecting a random sample of the points from that design as your sample.

Steve Buckland

messages.subject: Re: broods as clusters?
messages.body_plain:
I have communicated with David individually on this subject.  You'll get
the same answer whether you partition or not as long as f(0) is the same
for single and broods.  If the f(0) are not the same then you have
size-bias.  I sent him a simple excel spreadsheet that showed that you
can partition the average sbar into singletons and the average sbar for
non-singletons to show how the partitioning would give the same answer.
If you want that sheet to understand it further I suggest you contact David.

regards --jeff
